prompt: Fewer and fewer people nowadays use hand like pen, pencil and brush. What are the reasons?It is positive or negative development.
essay:
In an increasingly digitalised world, fewer people are using traditional writing implements such as pens, pencils and brushes in their daily lives. This shift is largely driven by the widespread availability of digital devices and the convenience of electronic communication. Although the decline of handwriting has some disadvantages, I believe it is predominantly a positive development because it improves efficiency and facilitates communication.

The principal reason for this trend is the rapid adoption of digital technology. Smartphones, tablets and computers allow people to write, edit and share information almost instantaneously, making traditional handwriting less necessary than it once was. In workplaces, for instance, emails, word-processing software and digital documents have largely replaced handwritten correspondence and paperwork. Similarly, students increasingly use laptops and tablets to take notes and complete assignments because digital text can be edited, stored and accessed more conveniently. Another contributing factor is the growing popularity of online communication, through which messages can be sent to large numbers of people within seconds without the need for handwritten notes or letters.

This development has both drawbacks and advantages, but its benefits are more substantial. On the negative side, reduced handwriting practice may weaken people's ability to write neatly and fluently by hand, particularly among younger generations. It may also diminish the cultural value attached to handwritten letters, personal notes and traditional forms of calligraphy. Nevertheless, digital writing offers considerable practical benefits. It is faster, easier to modify and considerably more efficient for storing and sharing large amounts of information. Moreover, digital tools can improve accessibility for people who struggle with conventional handwriting and enable communication across geographical boundaries.

In conclusion, the decline in the use of pens, pencils and brushes is primarily the result of technological advancement and the increasing dominance of digital communication. While this trend may contribute to the gradual loss of some traditional writing skills and practices, I consider it a largely positive development because of the greater efficiency, accessibility and convenience that digital communication provides.
